name: ngEHT closure-constrained imaging
description: reconstruct(visibilities, array_metadata, noise) -> nonnegative square image in Jy per pixel with calibrated total flux. Source data supply uv wavelengths, amplitudes, signed closure triangles and phases. Independent direct Fourier transform checks amplitude/closure likelihood and fixed-centre, resolution-matched image NRMSE. Source models/schedules split. Official ngEHT permission required before staging restricted challenge files.

papers.title: Interferometric Imaging Directly with Closure Phases and Closure Amplitudes
papers.task_relation: The local ngEHT task reconstructs a nonnegative, flux-constrained image from amplitudes and closure phases. Its fixed resolution, source data, and image score form a restricted adaptation; it does not use all closure-amplitude methods or reproduce an observed black-hole image.
papers.primary_goal: Develop interferometric image reconstruction using closure quantities that are insensitive to station-based calibration errors.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Recover astronomical brightness structure from sparse interferometric observations with calibration-robust constraints.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Reconstructing images despite station calibration uncertainty is the direct astronomical inverse problem studied in the paper.
science_relevance.reason: The source solves an observational imaging problem; importance is not inferred from an ngEHT dataset description.
